assertions.name: C3_finite_type_EXCLUDED_max_omega_is_4
assertions.source: P3 CONFIRMED, and this is the result. The source says each eq-(98) entry is ONE Stokes constant at ONE Borel singularity iota_{i,j} -- a multiplicity at a single charge, not a count of distinct objects. Gabriel's bijection gives every positive root multiplicity exactly one, so a finite-type quiver has max Omega = 1. The datum has max |Omega| = 4. Scope-(b) structural exclusion: the cited invariant is Gabriel's bijection itself

assertions.name: C4_eq100_mirror_holds_and_is_count_breaking
assertions.source: P1 CONFIRMED. The source states eq (100) for the q-series coefficients S^(k); it is checked here on the eq-(98) constants and holds. phi = (1 2) is sign-reversing, hence count-breaking -- exactly what the Lean QuiverMirrorAutomorphismExcluded requires of any mirror implementation that reads (4,3). The source's own symmetry and the corpus's proved exclusion agree independently

assertions.name: C5_both_sibling_answers_are_void_same_reason

assertions.name: C7_antisymmetry_discriminates_nothing
assertions.source: Pre-empting the next available misreading, which is the same shape as the two already made. eq (98) IS antisymmetric, and an antisymmetric integer matrix indexed by three objects looks exactly like a quiver exchange matrix -- reading it as one gives arrows 4+3+3 = 10 on 3 nodes, a DIFFERENT answer from H's 3. But BOTH readings entail antisymmetry (CPT sign on Stokes constants vs B_ij = -B_ji by definition), so observing it separates them not at all; there are 729 antisymmetric 3x3 integer matrices with entries in [-4,4] and eq (98) is not distinguished by being one of them. The source says Stokes constants; that is the only thing deciding it here

description: qou-q9ih D1-b. This probe VOIDS THE PREMISE of its sibling dt_d1b_arrow_count_forced_by_gabriel_probe, which has now given two different arrow counts ('forced to 0 or 1', then 'in {0,1,2}'). Both presuppose the corpus's (4,3) datum counts INDECOMPOSABLES of a finite-representation-type quiver. Checked against the source for the first time: GGM arXiv:2012.00062v3, held in this repo, says under eq (96)/(97) that each eq-(98) entry is 'the Stokes constant associated to the Borel singularity iota_{i,j}' -- a MULTIPLICITY AT ONE CHARGE. Gabriel's bijection gives every positive root multiplicity exactly one, so any finite-type quiver has max Omega = 1; the datum has max |Omega| = 4. NO finite-type quiver carries it at any rank with any arrow count, so both sibling answers are void -- scope-(b), the cited invariant being Gabriel's bijection itself. What the source gives back: the index set is THREE sigma-series so the singularities run over SIX ordered pairs, and S+ and S- populate exactly the two OPPOSITE ORIENTATIONS of the same three unordered pairs {12,13,23} -- the bar-conjugate ray pair is the two orientations of a 3-node complete graph, not two arbitrary stability rays. Neither that fact nor eq (100) was previously recorded in this corpus. eq (100)'s mirror phi = (1 2) is SIGN-REVERSING, hence count-breaking, agreeing independently with the Lean QuiverMirrorAutomorphismExcluded. The obvious reading V=3 with 3 arrows is recorded as a LABELLED HYPOTHESIS with its disconfirmation test, NOT as a result: KS arrows are the Dirac pairing on charges, not the populated singularities.
